topics.topic: How append_audit obtains the owning operation's single captured timestamp
questions: How does append_audit obtain the owning use case's already-captured instant so that the business record and audit record have the same timestamp without a second clock read?
How does append_audit use the owning operation’s single captured instant when that instant is not an input and append_audit supplies occurred_at itself?
How does `append_audit` obtain the owning operation’s single captured instant without taking a second clock reading or accepting `occurred_at`?

quotes:
`audit_writer` supplies `audit_id` and `occurred_at`; callers
  cannot supply either.

Each operation
reads the clock once (`datetime.utcnow()`), and that one instant supplies every
portal-owned timestamp it writes (event times such as `created_at`,
`received_at`, `occurred_at`, `revoked_at`) and every current-time comparison
that decides the validity of those writes or of persisted records.
judgement.why: The audit writer must supply occurred_at, but the owning operation must supply every written timestamp from its single clock reading, and no input conveys that instant.

questions: When list_project_progress reads an archived project with no manual budget, may it create the empty manual budget and its audit?
May ensure_manual_budget create a BudgetVersion and audit record while the Registry project is archived?
May `ensure_manual_budget` create and audit a manual budget version when its `AuthorizedProjectContext` is for an archived project?

quotes:
The one write that is not refused for an archived project
is the empty manual budget version (with its audit) that
`ensure_manual_budget` creates, also when `list_project_progress` reads a
project that has none.

An archived Registry project is readable and refuses every mutation of its
budget, snapshot import and activation, expense, document, progress, payment
and photo records (accepted `rules.registry_status_policy`: archived reads,
never mutates).

questions: What process outcome is required when configuration loading or bootstrap storage fails?
Must every invocation terminate with one of the four specified exit codes, or may infrastructure failures escape and produce another process status?

judgement.why: This is the same configuration-or-storage-failure exit-outcome question already answered by P1, and the relevant text has not changed.

precedent.topic: CLI exit outcome for configuration-loading or storage failures
quotes: A configuration or storage failure is none of the four outcomes: the operation raises it and returns no exit code, and the failure status the host process then ends with is outside the closed contract of A29.
precedent.why: The operation explicitly guarantees no returned exit code for these failures and leaves the resulting host-process status outside the four-outcome contract.

topics.topic: How validated runtime settings are delivered to identity use cases
questions: How do authenticate_staff and the other use cases receive the validated deployment settings when neither their operations nor api.create_app accept RuntimeSettings and PortalStore owns persistence only?

quotes:
Environment values are read once, by `runtime_settings`,
into `RuntimeSettings`; other modules read `config.*` constants or the
settings they are handed, never the environment, with two exceptions
kept from the running service: `registry_gateway` reads
`REGISTRY_BASE_URL` at each Registry call (A6, A30) and `binary_storage`
reads `BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT` and `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES` at each binary
read, each refusing that call when its value is missing or unusable
(Factory code `adapters/registry_gateway.py` `_registry_url`,
`adapters/binary_storage.py`; owner 2026-11-06: current service
behaviour accepted; technical decisions delegated).
The one `PortalStore`.

R0-06 (fixed expiry of
`config.staff_session_ttl_hours`, twelve hours),
`RuntimeSettings` supplied by the caller.

R0-10 and R0-11: exactly one `PortalStore` from `settings.database_url`; one
inner application from `api.create_app`; liveness at `/health/live` and
readiness at `/health/ready`, each answering exactly `HealthStatus`; the
transport guard installed before mounting; the inner application mounted at
`/api` and then at `/`.
judgement.divergence: One implementation injects the deployment RuntimeSettings through an unstated channel and issues sessions using the configured TTL; another has only the documented default available and issues twelve-hour sessions, which the staff member and later authorization checks notice.
judgement.why: The texts require use cases to consume deployment settings they are handed but fix api.create_app's input to only PortalStore and name no other delivery path.

witness.initial: The deployment configures staff_session_ttl_hours to one hour instead of the twelve-hour default.

create_runtime_app constructs PortalStore and calls api.create_app.
A staff member invokes authenticate_staff through the API.
outcomes: The configured settings reach authenticate_staff through an unstated mechanism and the session expires after one hour.
authenticate_staff uses the documented twelve-hour value because only PortalStore reaches the application.
witness.observer: The staff member and subsequent session authorization checks.
basis: `module:staff_identity`. Sign a staff member in with email and password and issue a session.

`StaffSessionGrant`: session id, staff id, role, the session token in
plaintext (returned once) and `expires_at`.

topics.topic: Whether foreign-origin viewer entry requests must be rejected before access-code exchange
questions: Must POST /auth/viewer/enter from a foreign Origin be refused before the route, or may it exchange a valid access code for a session?

quotes:
Viewer browser routes accept only that cookie, and
mutating viewer requests are refused unless they come from the portal's own
public origin.

The origin check covers the one viewer mutation the viewer
session cookie authenticates, the viewer logout. Viewer entry presents an
access code rather than that cookie: it is limited by the entry rate limit,
not by origin, so an entry from another origin reaches the route.
judgement.why: Viewer entry creates a ViewerSession and is therefore a mutating viewer request, yet State 5 expressly exempts it from the required public-origin check.
